gh "pr" "create" "--title" "feat: load skills (SKILL.md), list them in the system prompt, and expand /skill:<name>" "--body" "Closes #54.

pi-action now loads [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) the way pi's coding agent does. Docs: [`docs/skills.md`](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/blob/feat/skills/docs/skills.md).

### Discovery (`src/skills.ts`)
- Searched in this order, and the first skill with a name wins (the others get a warning):
  1. Packages: those in `extensions`, then those in the new optional **`skills`** input (same spec syntax). Each package gives its `pi.skills` list, or else its `skills/` directory. Packages in `skills` are installed but **their code never runs**. A package that has only skills no longer gets the "has no pi extensions" warning.
  2. Project: `.pi/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`, **only with `trust_project: true`**. Without it, the log says `Not loading the skills in .pi/skills: trust_project is off`.
  3. User: `<agent_dir>/skills/`, when `agent_dir` is set.
- Skills are found recursively. A directory with a `SKILL.md` is a skill, and its subdirectories are its resources, not more skills. Hidden directories and `node_modules` are skipped.
- Frontmatter is checked against the Agent Skills rules. `name` is required, uses `a-z0-9` and single inner hyphens, is at most 64 characters, and must match the directory name. `description` is required and at most 1024 characters. A skill that breaks a rule is skipped, and the warning gives the reason. `disable-model-invocation: true` keeps a skill out of the prompt list but still allows `/skill:name`.
- There's no YAML dependency. A small parser handles top-level scalars: plain, quoted, multi-line, and `|`/`>` blocks. Nested maps are ignored.
- Setup log line: `Skills: release (project), deploy (project, /skill:deploy only), changelog (xyz-skills)`.

### Prompt section
- New built-in pi-durable extension `pi-action` (`src/builtin-extension.ts`). It is installed after `coding-tools` and before the user's extensions, so they can `wrapSection("available_skills", …)`. Its name is reserved. #53 can add the AGENTS.md section to it.
- `available_skills` uses the wording from the issue, with absolute locations and XML escaping. The section is left out when no skill is listed.
- The text is memoized per run. When the model sees `typescript` and no `read` tool (pit-only, #52), it says `workspace.read` instead of "the read tool".

### `/skill:<name> args`
- Replaces the task with `<skill name=… location=…>References are relative to <dir>.\n\n<body>\n</skill>\n\n<args>`, as pi does. This works in first messages, follow-ups and `prompt`, but not in answers. It runs before prompt-template expansion.
- An unknown name sets a new `Trigger.rejected`. `ThreadConversation` doesn't submit the trigger. Instead it replies with an error listing the skills, gets the 😕 reaction, and records it as posted so later runs don't post it again.
- The log shows `▶ … /skill:release 2.4.0 (skill from project)`. The comment entry stores `skill` and `typed`.

### Tests
- `src/skills.test.ts`: frontmatter parsing, discovery order and recursion, name collisions, each validation rule, section text and escaping, tool-aware wording, memoization, expansion and rejection.
- `src/extensions.test.ts`: `pi.skills` versus `skills/`, the `skills` input (including npm install and not running code).
- `src/run.test.ts`, end to end: system prompt, first-message and follow-up expansion, the `trust_project` gate, an unknown-skill error reply that isn't posted again.

### Docs
New `docs/skills.md`. Also updated: README (input table, docs table), `docs/extensions.md`, `docs/security.md` ("Skills from the repository"), `docs/prompts.md`, `docs/how-it-works.md` and CONTRIBUTING (source map).

### Known limitation
A run whose only request is an unknown `/skill:` still opens the thread, because `Thread.open` commits. The next request on that issue is then sent as a follow-up without the issue's context. Other runs that fail early on a new thread behave the same way.

`npm run check` passes (439 tests)." "--base" "main" "--head" "feat/skills"
